candidate_078.name: locally revocable source-transfer gate with reliability-conditioned acquisition
candidate_078.mechanism_hypothesis: Reuse prior scientific systems only through a source-specific reliability model trained on observations from the current target. Let transferred evidence affect the target prior, prediction and acquisition only in regions where the source has demonstrated local predictive validity; automatically fall back to target-only learning where reliability drops. Treat source trust as spatially revisable rather than globally on/off, and require diversity/pruning when many sources are available to limit negative transfer and overconfidence.

primary_evidence.source: Eduardo González-García et al., PhaseTransfer: A transfer learning framework for efficient phase diagram mapping, npj Computational Materials 12, 279 (2026), published 2026-05-26.
primary_evidence.matched_synthetic_protocol: Across three synthetic phase-diagram families, methods were evaluated under identical sampling conditions across 50 independent runs with identical random initialization within each run. Each source has a paired weight GP trained from current-target observations to predict whether that source is correct at a location. Where reliability is low the informed prior reverts to the uninformed target baseline; where reliability is high transferred evidence contributes and acquisition shifts away from redundant boundary sampling.
primary_evidence.quantitative_results: On the sine-wave benchmark, Multi-Source PhaseTransfer required 57% fewer samples than vanilla active learning to reach 10% error and 56% fewer to reach 5% error. On the biological-condensate synthetic benchmark the reductions were 38% and 32%; on supramolecular copolymerization they were 67% and 37%.
primary_evidence.negative_transfer_stress_test: With at least two relevant sources, adding several irrelevant source diagrams had no considerable impact on final mapping efficiency; error curves clustered by the number of relevant sources. Performance approached or fell below vanilla only in extreme cases where irrelevant sources vastly outnumbered relevant ones and were simultaneously highly confident and wrong. This is direct evidence that target-observation-trained local reliability weights can suppress some bad transfer, while also defining a failure boundary.
primary_evidence.physical_autonomous_validation: PhaseTransfer was integrated into the PhaseXplorer autonomous microfluidic BSA-PEG condensate platform. Ground truth used 453 autonomous compositions. The transferred method reached 5% error after 2 batch iterations while vanilla active learning required 4, a twofold reduction in experimental burden on that single physical system.
primary_evidence.control_relevance: This supplies a science-domain positive control for candidate_077's proposed revocable cross-channel sharing layer: a controller can preserve separate acquisition objectives while allowing prior systems/channels to update a target only where target-side observations support local reliability. It also links naturally to candidate_072 measurement admissibility and candidate_076 fidelity discrepancy because trust is an explicit gate before transferred evidence changes acquisition.
primary_evidence.limits: The direct reliability gate is across related phase diagrams, not across simultaneous instruments, and the physical experiment covers one relatively simple BSA-PEG boundary. The negative-transfer stress test is synthetic and the paper does not isolate weight-model removal as a single matched component ablation. Extreme many-source confident-wrong regimes can still erase the advantage. The fixed reliability threshold tau=0.6 is not established here as a universal optimum.
